messages.subject: Re: Using subjunc and exactSNP in allele-specific expression analysis pipeline
messages.subject_clean: Using subjunc and exactSNP in allele-specific expression analysis pipeline
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sam,

Apologies for my slow reply.

I think in general you would expect reads containing the reference allele have a higher mapping percentage than those containing the reference allele, which may confound your allele-specific expression analysis. Subjunc might perform better than other aligners because of the better tolerance of mismatches, but if reads originate from highly repetitive regions it would be quite hard to map them correctly.

Subjunc converts "N" in the reference to "A", so replacing the nucleotide at SNP locus with N wouldn't help if your reference allele or variant allele is an A.

Output of exactSNP includes all alternative alleles it observes in the data, so you should be able to find heterozygous site from its output.

Hope this helps.

Best wishes,
Wei
